whatWorks: The palette is disciplined and exactly on brief: a near-black ground, a narrow iron-to-ash grey ramp, and a single warm ochre hue that never drifts into other colour. Nothing here needs re-picking.

The work is genuinely flat. There are no gradients, no cast shadows, no vanishing points and no fake lighting anywhere; overlapping translucent members produce tonal steps that read as material rather than as depth. That is the correct medium and must not be traded for modelling.

The recursion machinery is real and visible: in the diamond family (5003, 6444, 5789) a smaller generation is genuinely inscribed within the larger one, on the same centre. The production exists and only needs to be aimed at the right primitive and run deeper.
Placement and margin at rest are right in most seeds: the figure is centred, symmetric, and held clear of all four edges, so it reads as a discrete object and not a crop of a larger field.

findings.whatFails: The dominant member in eight of twelve seeds is a square rotated 45 degrees, and the remaining seeds are built from filled circles (5134, 5658, 6051, 6182), play-button triangles (5265, 5920, 6444) and a six-point star (5527, 6313). Not one token contains an axis-aligned rectangular bay.
findings.why: The brief asks for a colonnade seen head on and flattened into pure structure, and the direction names a nested series of rectilinear bays. A 45-degree lozenge is not rectilinear, it reads as a gem or a crest, and its tilt reintroduces exactly the sense of a rotated viewpoint the brief says to discard. Circles and stars carry no interval and no load, so the arcade reading is absent from the sheet entirely.
findings.specificChange: Remove the 45-degree rotation from the bay production and replace circles, triangles and stars with axis-aligned rectangles, so every generation is an upright rectangular bay sharing the frame's own axes. Restrict the primitive set to rectangles and straight members, and move the shape variety onto bay aspect ratio instead, spread across roughly 3:1 wide through 1:2 tall.
findings.keep: Keep the centred placement, the strictly flat no-perspective read, and the layered translucency that produces the tonal steps between overlapping members.

findings.whatFails: The outer member is drawn as a hairline of roughly 1 to 2 px at 256 in a mid-dark grey, while a large solid mid-grey mass sits inside it. On the 120px sheet the outer outline of 5789, 5003 and 6051 nearly disappears and the filled interior blob is the only thing left, so the loudest element in the frame is the interior, not the frame.
findings.why: The direction requires one dominant outer bay to command the frame with the inner generations descending as secondary structure, and asks for a result that feels load-bearing and slightly severe. The current contrast ordering is exactly reversed: the structural member is the faintest thing present and the incident inside it is the brightest, so the token reads as a fragile outline containing a blob rather than as an engineered run of supports.
findings.specificChange: Increase the outermost member's stroke to about 3 to 4 percent of the frame width, roughly 8 to 10 px at 256, and raise its value to the lightest ash in the ramp. Step stroke weight down by about 30 percent per generation inward so weight itself carries the recursion, and darken every interior fill toward the ground until no filled mass exceeds the outer member in contrast.
findings.keep: Keep the near-black ground and the narrow iron-to-ash range exactly as they are; do not brighten the ground or widen the ramp to buy this contrast.

findings.whatFails: The ochre is neither single nor innermost. 5134 carries four or more ochre blobs around the perimeter, 5396 carries about five ochre squares scattered through the pile, 5527 carries a symmetric ochre pair, and 5658 puts four ochre dots at the extreme corners of the frame with no structure near them at all. 6313's ochre is a tiny pair at the bottom that reads as dust at 120px.
findings.why: The brief and the palette intent both reserve one warm ochre accent for the innermost bay. Scattering it turns the accent into texture and destroys the only device that marks the centre of the recursion; in 5658 it is applied to the outermost elements, which inverts the meaning of the accent. A single reserved mark is also what makes the innermost generation legible once the interior articulation dissolves at browse size.
findings.specificChange: Restrict ochre to exactly one element per token and pin it to the innermost generation only. Remove every ochre mark that falls outside the second-innermost bay, and delete the corner dots in 5658 and the sub-pixel ochre pair in 6313 rather than shrinking them further.
findings.keep: Keep the ochre hue itself and its temperature against the iron greys; the colour choice is correct and only its count and position are wrong.

findings.whatFails: Stress adds mass instead of removing it: 5134 stress grows larger and gains circles until it nearly fills its cell, 5396 stress becomes a dense overlapping mush of squares, and 5003 stress gains an extra rotated square. Recovery is meanwhile almost indistinguishable from neutral in all four rows, with 5265 and 5396 differing only by a faint tonal shift.
findings.why: The brief states that under drawdown members are removed and the run opens out, and that in recovery the colonnade fills back in and the nesting deepens. The runtime does the opposite on stress and does nothing on recovery, so the one claim about market state that a viewer can check is false in one direction and unmeasurable in the other. It also destroys the structural margin, which the direction calls load-bearing rather than left over.
findings.specificChange: Invert the response: under stress remove the innermost one to two generations and widen the gap between the remaining bays by about 40 percent so the run visibly loses members and opens out, and under recovery add two to three generations inward while tightening the contraction ratio so depth of nesting is what changes. Require recovery to differ from neutral by at least one added generation, and cap the outermost bay's size so no state grows into the margin.
findings.keep: Keep the token recognisably the same token across all three states: the outer silhouette, the accent position and the centre must not move between states.

findings.whatFails: At 120px the outer silhouette is the same diamond in eight of twelve tokens, so 5003, 5789, 6051, 6182 and 6313 collapse into one family that is hard to tell apart, and 5265, 5920 and 6444 collapse into a second. What actually differs between tokens is the interior blob, which is the part that dissolves at browse size, and in 6051 and 6182 that blob resolves into a face with two eyes and a moon with a pupil.
findings.why: The direction states that tokens differ first in the silhouette of the bay member, then in symmetry order, then in run depth, and the thumbnail intent says the stepped silhouette of a nested run is what must survive at 120px. The current build inverts this: the silhouette is held constant and the variation is spent on interior articulation that the brief explicitly does not ask to survive. The accidental faces also break the severe, engineered register the brief asks for.
findings.specificChange: Move the primary variation onto the outer silhouette by spreading bay aspect ratio, member thickness and corner treatment across the seed range, using at least three distinct corner productions such as square, notched and stepped, so the outermost outline differs token to token at 120px. Reduce interior incident to at most two secondary generations and remove filled circular masses entirely so no token can resolve into a face or a sphere.
findings.keep: Keep the empty structural margin on all four sides and the strict symmetry of the figure; those are what make the object read as engineered rather than drawn.

overall: The colour, the flatness and the centred placement are right, and the recursive production plainly works, but the sheet is not yet an arcade. The dominant form is a 45-degree lozenge rather than a rectilinear bay seen head on, and where it is not a lozenge it is a circle cluster, a play triangle or a star, so interval and load, which are the entire subject of the brief, never appear. Weight is applied backwards: the outer member is a hairline that vanishes at 120px while a bright interior mass takes the frame, which inverts the stated focal hierarchy and makes the tokens read as fragile outlines around a blob. The ochre accent, which should be the single mark of the innermost bay, is scattered to the perimeter and in one seed to the extreme corners. The market rows fail in both directions at once: stress adds mass and crowds the margin where it should strip members and widen the interval, and recovery is visually identical to neutral where it should deepen the nesting. Most consequentially for browse size, the variation is being spent on interior articulation that dissolves at 120px while the outer silhouette is held constant, so eight of twelve tokens read as the same diamond and two of them read as faces. The fix is directional rather than a rewrite: square the bay to the frame's own axes, put the weight on the outermost member and step it down inward, reserve one ochre for the centre, invert the state response, and let the outer silhouette carry the difference between tokens.
